title: IOLANI PALACE

texts.text: IOLANI PALACE

This is a historical architectural drawing sheet from the Historic American Buildings Survey detailing the Iolani Palace in Honolulu, Hawaii. The sheet includes a site plan showing the palace's location relative to surrounding streets like Beretania Street and Hotel Street, along with a north arrow and scale in feet. Textual descriptions provide historical context about the building's construction by King Kalakaua, its architectural modifications over time, and its current use as a government building.
IOLANI PALACE
PALACE
U HAWAII
HONOLULU HAWAII

THE PALACE OF VICTORIAN MODIFIED CLASSIC DESIGN WAS BUILT AS THE RESIDENCE FOR HAWAII'S MONARCHS BY KING KALAKAUA AT A COST OF $300,000. THE ORIGINAL DESIGN WAS BY ARCHITECT T.J.BAKER (JULY 1879 - JANUARY 1880) ARCHITECT C.J.WALL CONTINUED THE WORK (JANUARY 1880 - DECEMBER 1880) AND THE BUILDING AND INTERIORS WERE COMPLETED (IN LATE 1882) BY ARCHITECT ISAAC MOORE.

THE BUILDING WAS CONSTRUCTED WITH EXTERIOR WALLS AND MAJOR CROSS PARTITIONS OF BRICK. OTHER PARTITIONS WERE FRAMED OF WOOD. FOR THE LANAIS, CAST IRON CLASSIC COLUMNS SUPPORTED BRICK ARCHES AND WALLS. FOR FLOOR FRAMING THERE WAS LIMITED USE OF IRON GIRDERS SUPPORTING WOOD JOISTS. ROOF FRAMING WAS OF WOOD. IN 1929 - 31 THIS STRUCTURAL SYSTEM WAS REPLACED WITH STEEL FRAMING AND REINFORCED CONCRETE, BUT INTERIORS WERE PRESERVED.
THE ORIGINAL EXTERIOR BRICK WALLS WERE FACED WITH CEMENT PLASTER COMBINED WITH CAST CONCRETE DECORATIVE UNITS; SAND
FINISH PAINT WAS APPLIED TO CEMENT, CAST IRON AND WOOD TRIM.
THE INTERIORS WERE FINISHED WITH THE FINEST TRIM AND
MOULDINGS OF PLASTER AND NATIVE WOODS. FROM THE BEGINNING
THE BUILDING HAD MODERN PLUMBING AND A TELEPHONE SYSTEM;
IN 1887 GAS LIGHTING WAS REMOVED AND ELECTRIC LIGHTING INSTALLED.
WITH THE OVERTHROW OF THE MONARCHY IN 1893 THE PALACE
BECAME THE EXECUTIVE BUILDING AND IS PRESENTLY USED FOR
RECORDED BY
